blocks.text: The Futaba S3003 Standard Servo Motor is a widely used and reliable servo motor designed for general-purpose use in a variety of hobbyist and professional applications. Known for its precision, durability, and affordability, the S3003 is commonly used in RC vehicles, robotics, automation systems, and DIY electronics.

This servo features plastic gears with precise control over its movement within a 0° to 180° range. It operates on a voltage range of 4.8V to 6.0V, compatible with most microcontrollers including Arduino, Raspberry Pi, and ESP32. The S3003 includes a 3-wire cable for signal, power, and ground, making it easy to connect and control.

Whether you’re building a basic robot, adding motion to a model, or creating a simple automated system, the Futaba S3003 offers a cost-effective and dependable solution. blocks.text: A 5-watt, 10 kΩ cement (ceramic / “cement type”) resistor looks like a small block of engineering compact, solid, and matter-of-fact. The body is a hard, molded ceramic (often high-alumina) with the resistance element embedded or coated and the termination caps firmly attached. Its surface is utilitarian: usually a neutral color, sometimes with painted markings that identify its resistance and tolerance. The leads emerge straight from the ends or from metal caps, ready to be soldered or mounted.

Put it into a circuit and the resistor does exactly what it promises: it converts electrical energy into heat in a predictable way. As current flows the body warms, heat spreading through the ceramic and into the surrounding air or a heatsink. Under steady load it gives off warmth rather than drama a quiet, dependable thermal presence. You can sense its role by touch (carefully): warm but not glowing, steady rather than spiky.

Mechanically the component feels durable: the ceramic and cement protect the internal element and the terminals are rugged. It’s the sort of part you install and then forget about until service or troubleshooting requires you to check it. In many designs it’s a backbone doing the heavy, unglamorous work of limiting current or dropping voltage while quietly enduring thermal and electrical strain.

When ammonia is present in the environment where the sensor is located, the conductivity of the sensor increases with the increase of ammonia concentration in the air. A simple circuit can convert the change in conductivity into an output signal corresponding to the gas concentration. The MQ137 gas sensor has high sensitivity to ammonia gas and is also ideal for monitoring other organic amines such as trimethylamine and ethanolamine. This sensor can detect various ammonia containing gases and is a low-cost sensor suitable for various applications.

The Mini LED Traffic Light Display Module (Red/Yellow/Green) is a compact simulation module featuring three high-brightness 8mm LEDs arranged like a real traffic signal. Each LED is driven independently through its own control pin, making it a popular teaching aid for traffic-light and sequencing projects with Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi boards.

Common Cathode Wiring: A shared ground pin keeps wiring to a microcontroller simple.

It is ideal for classroom demonstrations, traffic-light simulations, and any project that needs a simple, ready-made three-color signal indicator.

The Arduino Leonardo R3 Development Board with USB Cable is a microcontroller board built around the ATmega32U4, the first Arduino board with USB communication built directly into the chip instead of a secondary USB-to-serial converter. This lets it appear directly to a computer as a mouse, keyboard, or virtual serial port, making it ideal for HID and USB-interfacing projects.
Microcontroller: ATmega32U4 running at 16MHz with native USB support built into the chip.
Operating Voltage: 5V, with a recommended input voltage range of 7-12V through the DC jack.
Enhanced Pinout: 20 digital I/O pins (7 of which support PWM) and 12 analog inputs.
Native USB HID: Can act as a USB keyboard, mouse, or joystick directly, without an external USB-to-serial converter.
